newsitem.title: UK: Licht sees 97/98 world sugar output near to 96/97.
newsitem.headline: Licht sees 97/98 world sugar output near to 96/97.

text.p: World sugar production should reach 123.37 million tonnes raw value in 1997/98, little changed from the 123.32 million expected for 1996/97, German statistician F.O. Licht said on Thursday.
Asia was expected to continue its decline and production was forecast at 36.34 million tonnes after 37.12 million in 1996/97.
But sugar output in South America was expected to increase to 22.16 million tonnes from 20.97 million.
The cane sugar sector would account for 86.97 million tonnes, almost back to its 1995/96 level and a recvoery from the 85.43 million seen in 1996/97, Licht said.
"While production is expected to show little change from 1996/97, offtake will continue to grow and the build up of stocks could come to a halt in 1997/98," it said.
"With a little bit of luck, exporters can even look forward to a modest decline in stocks which should support world prices although much will depend on regional developments."
